title: When a number becomes the goal
summary: Goodhart's law: when a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure. People optimize the number instead of what it was meant to show.
evidenceNote: Goodhart's law is an observation, not a precise scientific law. The famous 'cobra effect' anecdote is poorly documented; the Hanoi rat bounty of 1902 is better supported by historical research.

scenes.text: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.
It's called Goodhart's law, after economist Charles Goodhart. This popular wording comes from anthropologist Marilyn Strathern.
Reward a number, and people optimize the number.

scenes.text: You may know the 'cobra effect': bounties on cobras supposedly led to cobra farming.
scenes.reveal: Historians have found little evidence it actually happened.

scenes.text: A documented case: Hanoi, 1902. Officials paid a bounty for every rat tail.
scenes.reveal: Rats were spotted without tails — released, perhaps, to keep breeding.

scenes.text: Use several measures — and keep asking what the number is for.
